findings.reason: the census row granularity is this node's whole deliverable, and an undefined unit lets a worker emit a census that reads complete while omitting or merging the rows the surviving-section step depends on.
findings.text: §6's measure is "one row per named item", but its next sentence speaks of "the restore row" as a unit, and the §2 `paid-identity-deletion-protection` row it refers to carries three separately-stateable items (the partial restore, `f-pidp-the-restore-cli-re-arms-the-deletion-it-exists-to-prevent`, and `f-pidp-004`), while the `sn-lifecycle-integrity` §5 row names seven footguns; "one row per named item" therefore does not pin a granularity, so the census can satisfy the wording while collapsing distinct verdicts into one row (or, read as one row per `f-*` id, silently omitting the rows that name no id, e.g. "43 of 117 produced-name divergences" and "Three properties the schema and the live graph disagree about")

findings.reason: the sentence reads as sequencing guidance rather than the node's measure, and a worker will complete on the census artifact that precedes it.
